Hi Ellen — thanks for the details and the PDF.

Summary of next steps from our side:
1) I will open an internal support case (SC-9128) and engage Engineering + Security for a targeted conversation exclusion.
2) We need an explicit confirmation from your legal team that this request covers all Redwood-retained telemetry for that conversation id (audit logs, traces, and per-request telemetry). If Samir can reply to this thread confirming: "EverHealth authorizes Redwood to remove the conversation conv-ever-20260517-17 and associated telemetry recorded under RQ-SILVER-99," we can proceed.
3) We will redact the conversation from customer-visible logs and remove related request-level telemetry. For compliance/audit we will produce a redaction report with a hashed record of the operation and a timestamp.
4) Estimated timeline: 48 business hours from legal confirmation and acceptance of the redaction artifact. Longer if escalation to Privacy Ops is required.

Marissa — can you create SC-9128 and include the files Ellen attached? Ben — please advise on whether we need additional SOC2/Security approvals or if we can move forward once legal confirms.

Ellen — once we have Samir's confirmation I will add the case notes and route to Engineering for execution.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request to remove a single conversation from logs (RQ-SILVER-99)

Naomi — I reviewed the attached redaction request. We support targeted conversation excision as a one-off operation. A few technical notes for the runbook:

- Scope: we will remove the store-and-forward conversation payloads from the customer-facing request store, clear any in-memory caching keys, and remove associated per-request telemetry entries. We will NOT delete aggregated telemetry that has been de-identified and rolled into historical metrics.
- Audit trail: Security will generate a signed JSONL audit artifact listing the affected request IDs and a SHA256 digest of the removed payloads. That artifact will be stored in the customer's compliance vault (link to be provided) and attached to the JIRA SC-9128.
- Verification items we need from EverHealth: exact conversation id (conv-ever-20260517-17 — confirmed in Ellen's note), legal confirmation to proceed, and a business contact for acceptance of the redaction report.
- Estimated blackout window: the operation should be quick (<10 minutes), but full downstream propagation (removal from derived telemetry) may take up to 24 hours to reflect in all dashboards.

If Samir confirms in-thread authority, Security (Vivek) can sign off and Engineering will schedule a maintenance window within the 48-business-hour target.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
